newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Trade in S. Africa's Sentrachem suspended.
newsitem.headline: Trade in S. Africa's Sentrachem suspended.

text.p: Share trading in South African chemicals firm Sentrachem Ltd was suspended on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on Monday pending an announcement in the local press on Tuesday.
Some dealers said U.S. chemicals giant Dow Chemicals Corp is set to swoop on the firm with an offer of between 10.00 rand and 10.50 rand a share. Sentrachem's stock finished on Friday at 792 cents.
The offer would value Sentrachem's 193.87 million shares at about 1.94 billion to 2.04 billion rand.
Analysts said Dow had been attracted by the firm's Hampshire Chemicals Corp unit.
"(The Dow buy) is an extremely strong rumour, but no one is revealing their sources," said one analyst who declined to be named.
No comment from Dow Chemical or from Sentrachem was immediateley available.

Other market sources favoured a scenario whereby Sentrachem would sell its 50 percent stake in its Safripol joint-venture to either Hoechst South Africa Ltd, which owns the other 50 percent of Safripol, or an unnamed U.S. chemicals major.
Safripol makes high density polyethylene, polyprpylene and engineering plastics.
No comment from Hoechst South Africa was immediateley available.
"Out of the two rumours I would say the Safripol story is the most likely. But everything is still very speculative," an analyst said.
One analyst said the rumour was that a Safripol bid had been made that was highly aggressive and would greatly reduce Sentrachem's debt burden.
Sentrachem recently embarked on a programme to sell secondary businesses and on July 21 sold its NCP Yeast business to Bidvest for more than 40 million rand.

The move is part of a massive restructuring announced on June 24 whereby the firm is seeking greater focus and efficiency. The restructure also proposes the merger of its NCP and Karbochem units and plans to cut costs by 300-350 million rand at its Sanachem unit.
Sentrachem is also looking at listing an international specialty chemicals business anchored around Hampshire Chemicals in New York or London as part of the restructuring.

Sentrachem had a disastrous half year to end February in which one-off charges of 261 million rand due to forward cover contracts and restructuring costs at unit Sanachem plunged the group into a pre-tax loss of 257 million rand.

The restructuring programme aims to cut group debt by around one billion rand over the next 12 to 18 months. In the 1996 annual report, interest bearing debt was 885 million rand and non-interest-bearing debt was 1.852 billion rand.
